new-jersey.name: New Jersey

resources.label: NJDEP Office of Quality Assurance: Certified Laboratories (real-time Data Miner lists)
NJDEP: Private Well Testing Act (PWTA)

facts: NJDEP's Office of Quality Assurance says its certified-lab lists are generated in real time from its Data Miner site, including "Certified Drinking Water Labs" and "PWTA Laboratories Certified for Sampling".
Under the Private Well Testing Act, wells must be tested when a property with a well is sold, and landlords must test every five years (NJDEP PWTA page).
NJDEP says to confirm a lab's status from its certificate and Annual Certified Parameter List, or by calling OQA at 609-292-3950.
unverified: We did not copy the Data Miner lists because they change daily and are generated on request.
We found no NJDEP-published fee schedule for homeowner testing.

massachusetts.name: Massachusetts

resources.label: MassDEP: Find a certified laboratory for water testing
MassDEP certified laboratory search database
MassDEP: Private wells

facts: MassDEP's lab database is searchable by region, analyte and matrix; choose "Potable (DrinkingWater)" to limit results to drinking water.
Private wells in Massachusetts are regulated by the local board of health, which may set its own testing rules.
MassDEP says municipal treatment-plant labs generally do not take samples from private consumers other than local residents.
MassDEP's how-to page also links a spreadsheet of certified labs that offer services to private well owners.
unverified: mass.gov blocked our automated checker on 2026-11-02, so we have not yet transcribed MassDEP's private-well lab spreadsheet. We will add it as listings once we can verify it.
No state fee schedule; labs set their own prices.

north-carolina.name: North Carolina

resources.label: NC State Laboratory of Public Health: certified drinking water lab search
NCDHHS: Private well water testing FAQs

facts: NCDHHS says new private wells must be tested by the State Laboratory of Public Health (arranged through your county health department) or a state-certified commercial lab, within 30 days of completion.
For existing wells, NCDHHS says to contact your county Environmental Health program or a certified commercial lab; procedures and fees vary by county.
unverified: County fees vary and we have not collected them.
The state search lets you pick contaminants; we did not copy its results.
